articleTitle: Analysis of a particular working mode of S3R type regulator
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: This paper describes a possible particular working mode of S3R type regulator (with series or shunt switches). It occurs depending on payload power consumption when there is an integration in the regulation loop.

Author Keywords: Sequential Switching Shunt or Series Regulator (S3R)

articleTitle: Designing high frequency AC inductors using ferrite and molypermalloy powder cores (MPP)
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: This paper sets down the major considerations in the design of high frequency AC inductors. It describes two methods for designing the inductor— the area product method and the core geometry method. The two major effects of the inductor air gap, fringing flux power loss and increase of inductance, are discussed. Equations for the inductor design and a step-by-step design procedure are given. The use of a lumped air gap or a distributed air gap are discussed and a comparison of the losses resulting from these gaps together with experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Discharge detection in high voltage flight hardware
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: In high voltage flight hardware, design constraints like encapsulation, shielding, limitation of stored energy, limited number of applied components, etc, reduce the feasability of incorporating discharge detection sensors. Taking the Space Telescope Faint Object Camera high voltage cabling as an example, a simulation circuit was built on which discharge tests have been performed in air and in poor vacuum and proposals have been worked out for use of discharge detection sensors for future flight hardware.

articleTitle: The telecom 1 power subsystem from design to flight
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The unregulated power subsystem of TELECOM 1 is presented. Such a concept being totally new in Europe in the kilowatt range, many analyses and tests have been performed to assess some potential problem areas during initial development phase. The tests performed at system level during spacecraft integration, as well as initial in flight datas, show an excellent subsystem performance.

articleTitle: Exact continuous models of PWM regulators in both continuous and discontinuous conduction modes
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: In modelling PWM voltage-regulator dynamics the circuit is assumed to be a linear time-variant system and width-modulation action on the output fil ter is represented by a suitable set of impulse generators applied at each switching instant. Once the feedback-loop is open the "comb" function of its characteristic response can be expressed by means of a recursive matrix relation; the latter is Fourier-transformed thus achieving the continuous function G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">loop</sub> (jw). In the discontinuous conduction mode, the procedu re directly provides an analytic expression. In any case, this exact model requires mlnlmum compu ting resources and runs on most popular personal computers.

articleTitle: AC - busses for low earth orbits - a viable alternative?
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The paper recommends to incorporate one or two AC-busses in large space station power systems. Subject of the investigations is to provide a rational for the selection of AC-bus parameters. Wave shape related questions received particular emphasis.

articleTitle: Emploi de mesures d'impedance four la modelisation des accumulateurs nickel - CADMIUM
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Impedance measurements are performed on nickel­-cadmium cells over a wide frequency range (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> Hz). The diagrams are obtained using a galvanostatic mode for a quasi equilibrium state with a zero constant current intensity and a super­ imposed alternative current of small amplitude. The results are presented for a battery charged and discharged under standardized conditions. An equivalent electric circuit that best fits the experimental results is proposed.

articleTitle: The results of some end of life tests on the OTS battery
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The paper outlines the behaviour of the OTS battery in orbit and compares it with that of battery tested on the ground. The end-of-life tests on the in-orbit battery are also described.

articleTitle: Recovery circuit for snubber energy in power electronic applications with high switching frequencies
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: On the background of the general necessity for power electronic equipment to rise efficiency and to avoid power dissipation, especially in high switching frequency applications, a simple, reliable circuit is presented, which allows to recover snubber energy by using a self oscillating DC to DC converter. The features of the circuit are pointed out by measurements. The universal applicability is experimentally proved in three different types of power converters for electrical drives.

articleTitle: Current-injected control - An analytical investigation of current-injected control for constant-frequency switching regulators
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: State-space averaging and linearization are applied to the control law of current-injected, constant-frequency switching regulators, resulting in a bona fide two-loop system representation. As a theoretical goal, first-order behavior can be achieved with no right-half-plane zeroes. Actual performance may be limited by switching frequency interference considerations.

articleTitle: Power switching cell modelling - an easy way
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The notion of the controlled quantity and the analysis of the nature of the cell output voltage culminate in a cell model with extended frequency validity. It is of a simple, invariant topology, defined by the cell characteristic coefficients. Its generality and conceptual and mathematical simplicity qualify it as the most convenient, comprehensive and coherent means for the cell systematization and computer-oriented tabulation.

articleTitle: Improving the response time of a switching regulator using sensit and design/ASTAP
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The criteria of stability and response, as measured by the phase margin, and the frequency of the zero dB crossing are crucial to the successful design of the control circuitry of any power supply, including switching regulators. Using several unpublished techniques, these performance functions were written in a form suitable for ASTAP, so that their sensitivities with respect to the statistically specified elements and parameters could be calculated automatically and their corresponding best and worst combinations determined automatically. The same performance criteria were also used in DESIGN/ASTAP to systematically improve the response of the control circuitry of the switching regulator while maintaining its stability, i. e., its phase margin, at 45 degrees.

articleTitle: The giotto power supply subsystem
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The Giotto mission profile imposes peculiar constraints on the design of the spacecraft as well as on the design of the power subsystem. The Giotto PSiS is highly advanced both for the control concepts adopted and for the state-of-the-art components used. The overall subsystem reliability has been the other key design parameter. This paper describes the power subsystem configuration and the design criteria which have been adopted to satisfy the various requirements. The main test results, the problems encountered and the approach to their solution are also presented.

articleTitle: Design and development of a pyrotechnic arming and firing unit
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The design and development presented in this paper are the results of a programme, founded by ESA/ESTEC and perfonred by Christian Rovsing A/S af 1984, to design, build and test a representative section of a Pyrotechnic Arming and Firing unit and to establish an overall pyrotechnic system design concept, which is carrr patible with Ariane and Space shuttle launchers and launch sites. The design is adaptable and re-usable on rrost spacecraft programmes and thus eliminates the necessity of redesign and requalification for different programmes and improves the confidence in the reliability.

articleTitle: MATPWR - a mission analysis tool for leo spacecraft power profiles computation
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Developed to compute the power profile of LEO satellites, this computer tool takes into account the stations visibility areas (ground based or GEO relays) the coverage of geographical zones defined by points, and logical conditions of equipments (swath angles, preheating, logical interdépendance). The results are visualized through power curves and earth maps.

articleTitle: Multi primary winding inverter with low harmonic content
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: In this paper a low cost and low power inverter for domestic and solar applications is proposed. The prototype carried out obtains a low harmonic content in the output voltage waveform due to the special multiprimary transformer together with the optimal delayed values for the switching transistors. Special requirements are selected in order to take in a wide range of protections.

articleTitle: The calculation methods of the short-circuit currents in three-phase bridge rectifier circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: This paper using matrix methods describes the calculation methods of external short-circuit currents in three-phase bridge rectifiers. A part of the methods is first introduced by the author.

articleTitle: Temperature derivative battery charge control
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: A new battery charge termination technique for Ni-Cd batteries will be presented, which is especially effective in low earth orbit application. End of charge termination is based on the temperature increase at end of charge using the temperature derivative detection principle. This makes the end of charge termination practically insensitive to environmental temperature, depth of discharge and solar array charge current fluctuation and guarantees predictable battery voltages, long battery cycle life and minimum thermal dissipation. It also requires about 30% less charging power compared to the conventional voltage-limited charging technique.

articleTitle: Amelioration du procede d'impregnation electrochimique d'electrodes d'hydroxyde de nickel
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Nickel hydroxide electrodes containing about 11g/dm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of hydroxide, with capacities of 3.6 to 3.8 Ah/dm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> may be prepared at 353°K by electrochemical impregnation. The reproducibility of the results are obtained by reajusting the pH before each preparation. The control of each electrode is done during two cycles of charge and discharge following the manufacture by means of a potential relaxation method.

articleTitle: An alternative for satellite power distribution
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: After a short presentation of the HIPPARCOS satellite, the electrical system trade-offs which have led to the use of an AC Power Distribution for HIPPARCOS, are exposed. The inverter and the AC/DC modules using power FET's and synchronous rectification are described. Based on the HIPPARCOS Experience, some conclusions are drawn at system level and a philosophy for future satellites is proposed.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic array simulation
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Two approaches to the simulation of photovoltaic arrays are described and compared. The first involves the use of a pilot panel and variable light source. In the second, characteristic array curves are stored in the memory of a microprocessor-based simulator. For the first approach, a stability analysis based on Popov's method is presented. Experimental resul ts are presented for both systems.

articleTitle: 2 30W TWTA Power supply design
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The electronic power conditioner (EPC) design for 230W RF 12 GHz TWTs is presented. Particular emphasis is devoted in evidencing the bus and tube interface problems, the technological aspects versus the very severe environmental requirements and the protection philosophy. In fact the EPC has to handle a very high power (~600 W), to provide outputs voltages up to 7.5 KV, to guarantee high stability of output parameters inside a very large operating temperature range (-35°C / +70°C). The major problems encountered during the development, the followed approaches and the main obtained results are outlined.

articleTitle: Application of MC2 control feedback for 12 GHz 20 W EPC for telecom satellite
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: We described an EPC (electronic power conditioner) developped for French Telecom administration for an 12 GHz 20 W TWTA (Travelling wave tube amplifier). • EPC1 requirements are submitted and the electrical design which used MC2 (currentcontrol- modulator) control is described with associated results. An simulation model is proposed. Particular technological points such High-voltage transformer, hybrid module and other particular EPC Technological are described. Some particulars interfacing problems given by the TWT such current cathode regulation and switching behaviour will be presented.

articleTitle: MARECS AND ECS. The first few years in orbit
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The paper contains a brief description of the MARBCS/ECS power subsystem and discusses the in­ orbit operation of the power subsystem. Array per­formance and battery operation are covered as well as a brief discussion of in orbit anomalies together with the preventive measures for follow­-on spacecraft.

articleTitle: Time domain analysis of an S<>3R system
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: A sequential switching shunt regulator system is analysed using the time domain method. Important parameters are specified and the effects of amplifier and loop delays are examined. System respnse to transients is modelled and a comparison of results is made.

articleTitle: Design and development of a current limited solid state hybrid switch
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The design and development of the first of a family of hybrid, low power, current limited, solid state switches is presented. This switch has a unique and novel thermal protection technique which ensures the FET temperature never exceeds a predetermined threshold level both under steady state and transient power dissipation operating modes. The design concept of the switch is briefly described and a test method using an infrared thermal imaging technique and test results which validate the concept are included. The paper concludes with a summary of future solid state switch developments using this design concept.

articleTitle: A computer analysis tool for evaluation of solar array design
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Developed to evaluate a solar array design, this computer tool is capable of modelization of Si and Ga As cells (as a function of physical parameters, temperature and radiation fluences), identification from measurements, evaluation of operating point with respect to given loads and to orbital position (LEO, GEO or GTO).

articleTitle: Digital structure of an autopiloting for asynchronous machine FED by PWM conyertor
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: In this paper, the authors present a simple but effective digital solution (hardware and software) for control and regulation of converter-fed electric machine. Precisely, a completely digital structure of a command module for an autopiloted asynchronous machine is shown. The machine is fed by a voltage source represented by PWM inverter and operates with variable frequency. An appropriate operation of this system during the different transient states in all four quadrants of the torque speed plane is desired.

articleTitle: Asynchronized DC/DC converter for the data telemetry system of intelsat VI(x)
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: ADC/DC converter adopting some new concepts about the synchronization of a free-running inverter is described. The DC/DC converter has been designed for Intelsat VI Satellite to supply CTU (Central Telemetry Unit) and RTU (Remote Telemetry Unit). The converter circuit is conventional, but emphasis will be placed on the synchronization technique which is characterized by its simplicity, reliability and also for the possibility of large use in space, military and commercial applications.

articleTitle: A new small signal A.C. analysis tool for space power systems
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: An interactive, menu-driven computer program has been developed to analyze the small signal performance of electrical power systems. The Small Signal AC (SSAC) program enables the analysis of an arbitrary power system configuration using generic components. A component may be specified in terms of canonical circuit parameters or by selecting the entire component from a library. New component models and empirical data can be incorporated in the SSAC analysis through the use of the general component options. The SSAC program computes bus impedances, two-port parameters, loop gains, and small signal transient responses.

articleTitle: Study of a resonant converter using power transistors in a 25KW x-rays tube power supply
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: This paper describes a converter whose purpose is to feed an χ-rays tube (25 KW, 140 KV) from the industrial main power supply (380 V, 50 Hz). The authors justify the structure of this generator that is constituted by an inverter using power transistors and a transformer-voltage multiplier set which are connected by a series resonant circuit. The control logic of the transistors gives them the dual properties of these of thyristors. An accurate analytical study of this system allows to predetermine the characteristics of this converter now in its industrialization phase.

articleTitle: Influence of the bus regulation on telecommunication spacecraft power system and distribution
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The power systems and the electrical distribution of existing geosynchronous telecommunication spacecrafts are evaluated through 13 typical examples. The comparative study put in evidence the advantage of limiting the bus voltage excursion for the payload.

articleTitle: A 20 GHz/30 W TWTA for olympus transponder
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: The 20 GHz/30 W TWTA is an on-board part of the communication equipment which has been conceived as a flexible element within different experiment and service demonstration; e.g. video-teleconference within two or more earth stations, tele-education, data and video transmissions. The TWTA design (Traveling-wave tube amplifier), described herein, has been designed by Selenia Spazio S.p.A. under a current ESA contract in the development of the Olympus program, the biggest advanced european program for telecommunications.

articleTitle: Design of high-voltage, high-power, solid-state remote
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Two general types of remote power controllers (RPC's), which combine the functions of a circuit breaker and a switch, were developed for use in direct-current (dc) aerospace systems. Powerswitching devices used in these designs are the relatively new gate-turnoff thyristor (GTO) and power metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFET). The various RPC's can switch dc voltages to 1200 V and currents to 100 A. Seven different units were constructed and subjected to comprehensive laboratory and thermal vacuum testing. Two of these were dual units that switch both positive and negative voltages simultaneously. The RPC's using MOSFET's have slow turnon and turnoff times which limit surge currents and voltage spiking from high di/dt. The GTO's have much faster transition times. All RPC's have programmable overload tripout proportional to I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and microsecond tripout for large overloads.

articleTitle: Spacecraft Orbital Power Evaluation (SCOPE)
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: A Fortran program for analysing the energy balance in a satellite power system during Transfer Orbit and other mission phases is presented. Piece-wise integration is employed for computation of average battery current as the spacecraft spins, instead of calculus, to give full visibility of modelling techniques and provide data for plotting composite current and voltage waveforms. The program models a general power subsystem circuit which it solves for current, voltage and battery depth of discharge at increments of theta (spacecraft attitude) and time. Most aspects of the simulation method are discussed, including flexibility, limitations and interpretation of results. Ways of defining battery capacity are also explained to clarify the battery model.

articleTitle: Modeling and implementation of a digitally controlled power converter using duty ratio quantization
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: A power converter control technique is described in which digital circuits, discrete proportionalintegral- differential feedback, and duty ratio quantization are used to provide dynamic regulation. A time domain computer modeling technique is presented. Analytical results are compared to experimental results. Digital methods for output current limiting and soft-start are described. Output quantization noise is discussed.

articleTitle: The ERS1 power system
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE Power Electronics Specialists Conference (ESA SP-230)
abstract: Under the auspices of the European Space Agency, the European Space industries are about to embark on a new application satellite programme, namely that of earth resources. This paper describes the conceptual design of the electrical power system for the power and energy demanding, ERS1 mission. The power system concept proposed for this low earth orbit application is based on that of the SPOT platform and consists of a battery defined power bus together with a solar array shunt regulator able to control on both battery re-charge current and a selectable end of charge voltage level.
